learner_operation: Form the augmented matrix of a nonsingular 2x2 system, normalize the first pivot, eliminate the lower-left entry, normalize the second pivot, and when requested back-substitute.

fixed_features.feature: Two variables, two nonsingular equations with nonzero first pivot
fixed_features.justification: All source cases and tutorial 2112d3af-1fb0-5a70-ab99-59931db99930 teach forward elimination without row swaps.

fixed_features.feature: Unit pivots and upper-right first-row coefficient retained
fixed_features.justification: Lesson ee4b134d-2908-5930-86bb-32537e0d8347 explains the standard method and easier back substitution; arbitrary REF is not the requested route.

fixed_features.feature: Five radio options and target-dependent matrix-only or matrix-plus-pair response
fixed_features.justification: All ten original banks use this contract.

answer_roles.role: Correct bottom-right value and its rank among distractors
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Solution values, signs and distractor relative ranks may vary independently while exactly one complete choice satisfies the equations.
answer_roles.observed: Values change but all ten coefficient signatures and source bank shapes are fixed. Nine tested families have a unique correct y rank fixed across six cases; q-10522 has duplicate y values.
Authored indices are fixed per family but actual UI hashes choice IDs into a new order; no delivered fixed-index finding.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Both supported by source; corresponding prompt, option form and explanation must agree.
answer_roles.observed: Five easy profiles and five moderate profiles retained, with source-specific target fixed. No unsupported swap of field contracts requested.

coverage.result: All ten source banks replay after presentation normalization. Six parameter cases per profile include four corners, source zero offsets and [1,2]. Correct matrices and solution stages verified independently.

Control: 45 shuffled candidates -> 40 distinct solution vectors -> 39 delivery survivors. All five profiles and negative/zero/positive y remain. Requested batch: 5 -> 5, four profiles, 4/5 rank shortcut success.

counterfactuals.change: q-73544: hold coefficients and h=1 fixed; change k=0 to k=1.
counterfactuals.expected: Equations and solution change from (x,y)=(0,-2) to (0,-1); rendered solution and native key must agree.
counterfactuals.observed: Prompts change from RHS (8,14) to (4,7); correct matrices and pairs update, all five choices grade correctly before and after. Both visually inspected. The incidental second-smallest rule persists.
counterfactuals.justification: The constant column is relevant evidence for elimination; affine translation changes y while x remains fixed. Correct coupling does not certify pedagogical variety.

counterfactuals.change: Reverse the complete choice array for the k=0 instance without altering mathematical values or key.
counterfactuals.expected: Same correct mathematical response, prompt and explanation despite changed layout.
counterfactuals.observed: Native grading accepts the same UUID and rejects all alternatives. UI screenshots show a different ordering but the same correct matrix and pair.
counterfactuals.justification: Option order is incidental to the mathematical criterion and is already shuffled by actual UI choiceOrder.

delivery.result: Conditional rank shortcuts survive every examined stage. Actual published records are not created; selection fixtures reproduce the easy-band algorithm with synthetic stable entity ordering. Unknown live learner histories or policy weights limit schedule predictions, not the rank invariant.

limitations: Only captured inventory basis 5576 was used; it contains ten original questions and no generated records, verified in inventory-review.json.
No actual future learner schedule or postpublication entity IDs are known; selection is inspected and reproduced under explicit fixtures.
Finite tests do not rule out all other shortcuts. The demonstrated rank invariant is algebraic: each option lower row is (0,1,c), so the author always replaces c by c+k.
No free-entry fields exist; native grading tests all radio alternatives. Canonical example supplies context, not a captured answer bank.
